benchmark.name: swe-interact
benchmark.amd64_patch_source: generated from the pin by fsa/redo/swe_interact/amd64.py (`python -m fsa.redo.swe_interact.amd64 patch`, 2026-10-17, A5.13 (1)): task.toml docker_image of the 38 tasks of amd64.patch_tasks() (the 20 Stage-1 subset tasks + the 25 swebenchpro tasks of A5.11; 7 overlap) -> tib/swe-interact-amd64:<task> (tags over 128 characters: task[:119]-<sha256[:8]>)
benchmark.amd64_patch_stage1_source: the layer-1 file in force 2026-09-28 .. 2026-10-17 (Stage 0/1/2 runs record it): amd64.expected_patch(subset_tasks()), the 20 subset tasks only; still reproduced byte for byte by that call (tests/test_redo_machine.py)
benchmark.amd64_images: built natively once by `python -m fsa.redo.swe_interact.amd64 build` (label tib.recipe_sha256 = sha256 of the recipe Dockerfile; build context = the task's environment/): deepswe and rf tasks = the published docker_image plus the task Dockerfile's instructions from its COPY repo_exec_server.py line on (for rf tasks that is the task Dockerfile verbatim, which starts FROM the published image); swebenchpro tasks = their own Dockerfile verbatim. Why: the benchmark's multi-turn run configs pass --force-build, and the published images lack repo_exec_server.py (the main container's command and health check) and the rf rubric verifier's dependencies, so they cannot start a multi-turn trial as published. rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11889, rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11891 and rf_task-696719205599a51110d4b40c (Debian 11) pin apt away from bullseye-security during their verifier-dependency step only (its pool returned 404 for python3-pip 20.3.4-4+deb11u2 on 2026-09-28; main-pool versions are installed instead; the pin file is removed afterwards). rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11889 and rf_task-696719205599a51110d4b40c (no node/npm in the published image) also get Harbor's opencode system dependencies (curl bash coreutils nodejs npm) at build time, bullseye-security read from snapshot.debian.org at 2026-09-01 (index identical to the live one), because the pool no longer serves any Debian 11 file and the installer's trial-time apt step failed (2026-09-29); likewise swebenchpro_instance_gravitational__teleport-f432a71a13e698b6e1c4672a2e9e9c1f32d35c12 (Debian 11, no node/npm; its sources name security.debian.org), found by auditing all subset images against the installer's check (command -v curl bash stdbuf node npm; the other images failing it are Debian 12, Alpine or Ubuntu 20.04, whose repositories still serve the packages). rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11891 also preloads a Node module (NODE_OPTIONS += --require /opt/tib/node-cpu-quota.js) that makes os.availableParallelism()/os.cpus() report the container's CPU quota (cgroup v2 cpu.max): Node reports the host's CPUs, so on a 64-CPU host Jest started 63 workers for its full-suite verifier in an 8- or 16-CPU, 16 GiB container and swapped (2026-09-29).

harbor.version_note: The benchmark commit (2026-06-30) predates harbor 0.17; the README installs harbor from git main. 0.16.1 (the release current at the commit) and 0.23.0 both accept task schema 1.3 with [[steps]], multi_step_reward_strategy and environment.mcp_servers, and both run each step as a fresh agent session (0.23.0: resume_trajectory defaults to false, the published run configs do not set it; 0.16.1 has no resume). 0.23.0 is pinned because the arm64 task tree was validated with it (oracle + 5-step nop trial) and it needs only the one-hunk multistep log-ownership patch on local docker.

patches.why: swe_benchmark_arm: chown logs before each step's outputs are archived (local docker, multi-step)

(1) reward.json {'reward': 0.0, 'error': '...'} from the final step's write_failure() is scored 0 instead of raising VerifierOutputParseError (Non-numeric reward) and failing the trial; (2) the stop-after-failed-step path also hands log ownership back before moving the agent dir (PermissionError in cleanup_empty_mount_dirs otherwise), and cleanup_empty_mount_dirs() catches PermissionError if a timed-out earlier step's lingering opencode process creates a root-owned git snapshot dir between prepare_logs_for_host() and docker compose down. (1)-(2a) seen on S_plumbing in Stage 0; (2b) seen on deepswe_returns-validated-error-accumulation S/stock/natural_r1 a1 (2026-09-29).

harness.reasoning_note: opencode --variant=high on @ai-sdk/google sends thinkingConfig {includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel: 'high'} (verified for all three rung models against a logging proxy for SWE-Together, same opencode version); the published gemini-3p5-flash-high_opencode.sh passes no variant, which yields thinkingLevel 'high' too. The official config installs opencode@latest; pinned here to the SWE-Together version.
harness.throttle_note: RedoOpenCode re-issues a step attempt that only produced Gemini backpressure errors and resumes (opencode run --session, 'continue' message) a step interrupted by one, including the mid-stream 503 that surfaces as HTTP 400 'Requests ending with a model turn are not supported'; backoff 15..300 s; at most 8 consecutive retries of attempts that completed fewer than 5 model calls (an attempt with >= 5 resets the count; Stage 0 M/S ran with the first rule, 8 retries per step). Same markers and message as the SWE-Together wrapper.

user_sim.backend: Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, called by the unchanged sidecar (LiteLLM provider openai/, the sidecar prefixes the model with 'openai/' and appends '/v1' to LITELLM_BASE_URL; the trailing '#' turns that '/v1' into a URL fragment, which the OpenAI client never sends, so requests go to .../v1beta/openai/chat/completions). No clone change. Verified 2026-09-27 with litellm 1.90.1: multi-round tool calls work; Gemini's thought signatures ride in tool_calls[].extra_content, which the sidecar's model_dump keeps and sends back.
user_sim.client: user-server sidecar (litellm==1.90.1, fastmcp==3.4.2 pinned), reasoning_effort=high (-> thinkingLevel high), max_tokens=32768, up to 6 private repo-inspection tool rounds per reply
user_sim.patient_retry: SWI_SIM_RETRY=1 (local patch): 10..300 s backoff, 9 retries on throttling/transient errors, before the upstream plain-completion fallback / last-resort reply
user_sim.deviation: 2026-09-27 (Gemini-only seats): official SIM_USER_MODEL is gpt-5.5 (OpenAI); the OpenAI key has no credit. gemini-3.1-pro-preview is SWE-Together's official simulator, so both benchmarks now share one simulator model. Its per-minute quota is small (429 at ~4 concurrent short calls) and is shared with the SWE-Together simulator: expect sidecar retries; keep total concurrent simulator calls of both pilots low.

rubric_grader.backend: Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint from inside the task container (evaluate_rubrics.py, openai SDK in /opt/venv); task.toml maps EVAL_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}, EVAL_BASE_URL=${OPENAI_API_BASE}, so the runner sets OPENAI_API_KEY to the Gemini key in Harbor's environment (no OpenAI key is passed anywhere)
rubric_grader.deviation: official grader is anthropic/claude-opus-4-5-20251101 through a LiteLLM gateway; no Anthropic key. Until 2026-09-26 substituted by gpt-5.5; since 2026-09-27 (Gemini-only seats) by gemini-3.5-flash (the judge seat, not an agent rung). The local patch sends max_completion_tokens=16384 and reasoning_effort=high (upstream sends max_tokens=2048). Applies to the 7 rf_* subset tasks only.

S.thinking: thinkingLevel=high (opencode --variant=high); thinking cannot be disabled on this model

G.thinking: thinkingLevel=low (opencode --variant=low): 'high' exceeded 180 s on a one-line prompt and the harness has 1800 s per-exec caps

stage1_caps_note: stage1_trial_cap: Stage 0 recommendation while the SWE-Together pilot shares the Gemini key (W 6, M 1, S 1); stage1_trial_cap_after_swt: once it has finished (W 8, M 4, S 2), pass --cap W=8,M=4,S=2; raise further only if a batch shows no 429. rf_* tasks: at most 2 concurrent (16 CPU / 16 GB each; pilot --max-rf).
